bibleSpine.kjv: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
bibleSpine.gloss: The section's cornerstone. The angel names the Saviour by His work: He saves His people FROM their sins — not merely from sin's penalty, and not leaving them IN their sins. The Hebrew Yeshua = 'Jehovah saves'; the salvation named is separation from the sin itself.

bibleSpine.kjv: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.
bibleSpine.gloss: The paired name explains the method. He saves from sin by being 'God with us' — Christ in the flesh, and by extension Christ in you (Col. 1:27). The Person indwelling is the power that saves from sin.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Old Testament promise Matthew 1:21 fulfils: redemption FROM all iniquities, not toleration of them. 'All' leaves no reserved sin under which the redeemed remain.

bibleSpine.kjv: Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds; And have put on the new [man], which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:
bibleSpine.gloss: Defines salvation as restoration of the divine image. The old man is put OFF; the new man is 'renewed... after the image of him that created him' — salvation reverses the fall by re-creating the image of God in the soul.

bibleSpine.kjv: To whom God would make known what [is] the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:
bibleSpine.gloss: Salvation is not a legal status only but a Person possessed. The mystery of the gospel is 'Christ IN you' — the indwelling Saviour is Himself 'the hope of glory,' the pledge of the finished work.

bibleSpine.kjv: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
bibleSpine.gloss: The mechanism of Christ-in-you. The old self is crucified; Christ lives the new life through the believer 'in the flesh' by faith. This is how salvation FROM sin's power is wrought — not by the man's effort but by an indwelling Life.

bibleSpine.kjv: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with [him], that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: The stated purpose of the cross applied to the believer: 'that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.' Salvation aims at ceasing to serve sin, not at forgiven continuance in it.

bibleSpine.kjv: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
bibleSpine.gloss: Grace's promise is deliverance from sin's DOMINION. A gospel that leaves men under sin's rule until death contradicts the very clause that defines being 'under grace.'

bibleSpine.kjv: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.
bibleSpine.gloss: The section term verbatim: 'made free from sin.' Freedom from sin is present-tense fact for the believer, issuing at once in a new servitude — to righteousness.

bibleSpine.kjv: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.
bibleSpine.gloss: Repeats 'made free from sin' and traces its fruit — holiness now, everlasting life at the end. The whole arc of salvation (power now, presence removed at last) hangs on this freedom.

bibleSpine.kjv: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
bibleSpine.gloss: God's own Son, sent in 'the likeness of sinful flesh,' condemned sin in the flesh so that the law's righteousness 'might be FULFILLED IN us.' The gospel's end is not merely imputed righteousness but righteousness wrought in the believer by the Spirit.

bibleSpine.kjv: Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin. And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: [but] the Son abideth ever. If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ diagnoses sin as bondage ('servant of sin') and promises real emancipation: 'free INDEED.' The freedom He gives is not nominal — it actually severs the slavery.

bibleSpine.kjv: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
bibleSpine.gloss: The section term verbatim. Christ saves 'to the UTTERMOST' — completely, to the last extremity of sin's hold. His unbroken priestly life guarantees a salvation that reaches all the way, not a partial rescue.

bibleSpine.kjv: And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ was manifested 'to take AWAY our sins' — removal, not mere covering. The sinless One works sinlessness: the taking-away is the purpose of the incarnation.

bibleSpine.kjv: He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.
bibleSpine.gloss: The stated purpose of Christ's coming: 'that he might destroy the works of the devil.' Sin is the devil's work; a salvation leaving that work intact fails the purpose for which the Son was manifested.

bibleSpine.kjv: Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is. And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.
bibleSpine.gloss: Glorification: at His appearing 'we shall be like him' — the last stage, salvation from sin's very PRESENCE. And the present hope of it 'purifieth' now: the future likeness works backward into present cleansing.

bibleSpine.kjv: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, [even] as by the Spirit of the Lord.
bibleSpine.gloss: The section term verbatim: 'changed into the same image from glory to glory.' The process of salvation — progressive transformation into Christ's image by beholding Him, wrought 'by the Spirit,' the restoration of Colossians 3:10 in motion.

bibleSpine.kjv: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ's self-gift aims 'that he might redeem us from ALL iniquity, and PURIFY' a people. Redemption and purification are twin objects — deliverance from sin's guilt and its defilement together.

bibleSpine.kjv: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do [them].
bibleSpine.gloss: The covenant promise underlying New Testament salvation: cleansing 'from all your filthiness,' a new heart, God's Spirit within 'and CAUSE you to walk in my statutes.' God Himself works the obedience — salvation from sin's power is a divine operation, not a human resolve.

bibleSpine.kjv: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.
bibleSpine.gloss: The goal of Christ's love for His church: to 'sanctify and cleanse' now and to 'present it to himself a glorious church... holy and without blemish' at last. The everlasting gospel ends in a people actually cleansed from sin, not merely accounted so.

symbolDefs.meaning: God saving man FROM sin — from its guilt (justification, the pardon of Matthew 1:21 / 1888 80.2), from its power/dominion (sanctification, Romans 6:14, 18, 22; John 8:36), and at last from its very presence (glorification, 1 John 3:2). It is the restoration of the image of God in the soul (Col. 3:10; 2 Cor. 3:18), effected by the indwelling Christ (Col. 1:27; Gal. 2:20), reaching 'to the uttermost' (Heb. 7:25). Not a legal status only but a Person possessed and a nature renewed; a gospel that leaves men under sin's dominion until death is not the everlasting gospel.
receipts: Matthew 1:21 — 'he shall save his people FROM their sins' (from them, not in them)
Psalm 130:8 — 'he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities'
Colossians 3:9-10 — the new man 'renewed... after the image of him that created him' (restoration of God's image)
2 Corinthians 3:18 — 'changed into the same image from glory to glory' (the process)
Romans 6:18, 22 — 'being then made free from sin' (from its power)
John 8:34-36 — sin is bondage; 'if the Son... make you free, ye shall be free indeed'
Hebrews 7:25 — 'able also to save them to the uttermost' (completeness)
1 John 3:2-3, 5, 8 — 'we shall be like him' / 'to take away our sins' / 'destroy the works of the devil' (presence removed; purpose of His coming)
Titus 2:14 — 'redeem us from all iniquity, and purify' (guilt and defilement together)
Colossians 1:27; Galatians 2:20 — 'Christ in you, the hope of glory' / 'Christ liveth in me' (a Person possessed, not a status only)

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: It is a message of salvation from sin. For before this time the same angel had foretold to Joseph the birth of this infant, and had said, “Thou shalt call His name Jesus; for He shall save His people from their sins.” Matthew 1:21.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner names the everlasting gospel exactly as the section does: 'a message of salvation FROM sin,' grounding it in Matthew 1:21. Corroborates the section thesis word for word.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: So the preaching of the everlasting Gospel is the preaching of Christ the creative power of God, through whom alone salvation can come. And the power by which Christ saves men from sin is the power by which He created the worlds.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner identifies the saving power as creative power — the same omnipotence that made the worlds now saves men FROM sin. Confirms that salvation from sin is a divine re-creation (the restoration of Col. 3:10), not human reform.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: And why does He make us free from sin?—In order that we may live free from sin. On account of the weakness of our flesh, we are unable to do the righteousness of the law; therefore Christ, who is come in the flesh, and who has power over all flesh, strengthens us with might by His Spirit in the inner man, that the righteousness of the law may be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner on Romans 6:18 and 8:3-4: Christ makes us free from sin 'in order that we may LIVE free from sin,' the righteousness of the law 'fulfilled in us.' Directly corroborates 'being then made free from sin' as a lived deliverance, not a legal fiction.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: Coming to Mount Sion,—to Jesus, the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling,—we become free from sin,—from transgression of the law.... we shall also find grace to help in time of need,—grace to help us in the hour of temptation to sin,... and we find cleansing from all sin.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner defines being 'free from sin' as freedom 'from transgression of the law' and 'cleansing from all sin' — grace that helps in the very hour of temptation. Confirms salvation reaches sin's power in the present, not only its guilt.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: The blessedness of the man unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works is the blessedness of sins forgiven, and of freedom from the power of sin. God will not impute sin to the man who lives by faith in Christ, so that Christ’s works are his works.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner joins the two dimensions the section distinguishes: justification ('sins forgiven') AND 'freedom from the power of sin' as a single blessedness. Confirms that imputed righteousness and deliverance from sin's power are inseparable in the gospel.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: The power of God is abundantly able to accomplish all for which it is given—the salvation of the soul, deliverance from sin and from the power of it, the reign of righteousness in the life, and the perfecting of the believer unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.... Many believe and receive the grace of God for the salvation from sins that are past but are content with that and do not give it the same place in the soul to reign against the power of sin.
witnesses.gloss: Jones spells out the whole arc: deliverance 'from sin AND from the power of it,' and rebukes the truncated gospel that receives grace only for 'sins that are past' while leaving sin's power in place. Directly corroborates the section's warning against a guilt-only salvation.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: “God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which has delivered you. Being then made free from sin, YE BECAME THE SERVANTS OF RIGHTEOUSNESS.” Thank the Lord for that! He says you are, and when He says you are, it is so.... Thank Him that you are delivered from sin, and thank the Lord that you are the servant of righteousness. He has made you so, for He says so.
witnesses.gloss: Jones preaches Romans 6:18 verbatim as present fact — the believer 'made free from sin' on God's own word. Corroborates the section term 'being then made free from sin' as a declared, received deliverance.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Satan was exulting that he had succeeded in debasing the image of God in humanity. Then Jesus came to restore in man the image of his Maker. None but Christ can fashion anew the character that has been ruined by sin. He came to expel the demons that had controlled the will. He came to lift us up from the dust, to reshape the marred character after the pattern of His divine character, and to make it beautiful with His own glory.
witnesses.gloss: White defines Christ's saving mission as restoring 'the image of his Maker' in man — 'reshape the marred character after the pattern of His divine character.' Confirms the symbol 'salvation' as image-restoration (Col. 3:10; 2 Cor. 3:18).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The central theme of the Bible, the theme about which every other in the whole book clusters, is the redemption plan, the restoration in the human soul of the image of God.
witnesses.gloss: White states the whole Bible's central theme as 'the restoration in the human soul of the image of God' — the exact definition the section gives to salvation. Corroborates that salvation FROM sin IS the restoration of God's image.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: He may talk of freedom, but he is in the most abject slavery.... Christ came to break the shackles of sin-slavery from the soul. “If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.” “The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus” sets us “free from the law of sin and death.” Romans 8:2.
witnesses.gloss: White expounds John 8:36: Christ 'came to break the shackles of sin-slavery,' making free 'indeed.' Confirms salvation as real emancipation from sin's bondage, not a nominal pardon that leaves the chains on.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: When Christ is formed within, the hope of glory, then the truth of God will so act upon the natural temperament that its transforming power will be seen in changed characters.... You will show that the authority of God over you is not in name only, but in reality and truth.
witnesses.gloss: White on Colossians 1:27: 'Christ formed within, the hope of glory' exerts a 'transforming power... seen in changed characters' — 'not in name only, but in reality.' Corroborates that Christ-in-you is a real transforming Presence, the very power of salvation from sin.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Jesus is the Sin-bearer. He takes away our sins, and makes us partakers of His holiness.... He is able to save unto the uttermost all who come unto God by Him. There is power in these precious promises, and we should cooperate with the working of Christ.
witnesses.gloss: White pairs 'takes away our sins' with 'makes us partakers of His holiness' and 'save unto the UTTERMOST' (Heb. 7:25) — removal of sin joined to impartation of holiness. Confirms salvation as both from sin and into Christ's own holiness, to the uttermost.

historyAnchor: The pioneer witnesses cluster around the 1888 Minneapolis message and the years following (Waggoner's The Everlasting Covenant, The Glad Tidings, and Waggoner on Romans; Jones's Lessons on Faith; White's 1888 Materials par. 80.2), when the Seventh-day Adventist reform emphasis on righteousness by faith as actual deliverance from sin — not imputed status only — came to the fore.
uncertainties: The verse tool returned the KJV of Col. 3:10 with 'new [man]' and 1 John 3:8 without red-letter markers; brackets in KJV text (e.g. '[man]', '[them]', 'even as by') mark supplied italics in the original AV and were preserved as returned. No red-letter (‹ ›) markers appear in the quoted spine except John 8:34-36, where they were stripped for the gloss but retained in the KJV field as the tool returned them.

Waggoner's 'Lessons on Faith' exists in the corpus under two authorship codes (LOF_EJW and LOF_ATJ); the two cited paragraphs (85.2 and 147.4) resolve under LOF_ATJ (A. T. Jones), so they are attributed to Jones. The volume is a joint Jones/Waggoner compilation, so a reader may see it cited under either name.

Direct-read of pioneer-book refcodes containing a decimal (e.g. 'LOF_ATJ 85.2') trips the CLI's FTS parser; the full paragraph texts were therefore pulled verbatim from the local corpus DB (/Users/cvr/.bible/egw-paragraphs.db) rather than via `bible egw <ref>` — the content matches the search-result snippets exactly.
